input.summary: Meridian's managed services portfolio spans seven active vendors; 97% of scope is maintenance-bound, blocking net-new delivery.
covers: Use-case delivery blockers tied to managed services

story.meaning: Meridian's managed services estate is dominated by legacy maintenance — Epic, Microsoft SQL marts, Tableau, SAS, and an outsourced analytics provider consuming ~80% capacity on upkeep — while AWS and Databricks remain aspirational targets with no certified foundation.
story.observed: Six active vendors confirmed; outsourced analytics managed services provider carries an 80% maintenance load. AWS and Databricks are scoped as target direction but lack medallion architecture, governed semantic layer, and identity spine. Contract terms are unevidenced across all seven vendors.
story.matters: The maintenance burden directly caps net-new delivery capacity. Every CEO/CFO/CIO priority use case — lakehouse, AI/LLM governance, call center optimization, cost transparency, payment integrity — is blocked until the target platform is stood up and the outsourced provider's capacity is rebalanced.
story.supports: Decision gate: Rebalance outsourced analytics contract scope and certify AWS/Databricks foundation before committing to any use-case delivery timeline. Evidence closure on contract terms and medallion architecture is the prerequisite.

findings: Outsourced analytics managed services provider absorbs ~80% of contracted capacity on maintenance of SQL marts, Tableau, Power BI, and SAS — leaving less than 20% available for net-new strategic delivery against CEO/CFO priorities.

AWS and Databricks are confirmed target-direction vendors but carry the highest contract risk in the portfolio: no medallion architecture certified, no governed semantic layer, no patient/member identity spine — blocking all five top use cases.

SAS analytics estate lacks governed model lineage and provider entity resolution, directly blocking payment integrity and leakage reduction from reaching decision grade despite CFO and Chief Experience Officer prioritization.

Epic Clarity and Caboodle integration to a governed lakehouse is unproven; until this closes, the unified clinical + claims lakehouse — the foundational prerequisite for four other use cases — cannot advance beyond planning stage.

chain: Outsourced Analytics MSP maintenance load → limits net-new delivery capacity → delays AWS/Databricks foundation build
AWS/Databricks foundation not ready → no certified medallion architecture → blocks Unified Clinical + Claims Lakehouse
No medallion architecture → no governed semantic layer → blocks AI/LLM Automation and all downstream use cases
SAS ungoverned lineage → provider entity resolution unproven → blocks Payment Integrity and Leakage Reduction
Epic Clarity integration unproven → no patient/member identity spine → blocks Provider Quality, Cost Transparency, and Call Center Optimization
relationships.note: The outsourced MSP's maintenance posture and the AWS/Databricks readiness gap are co-dependent blockers: rebalancing the MSP contract is necessary but insufficient without simultaneously certifying the target platform foundation, which is the prerequisite for all five CEO-priority use cases.

evidence.name: Managed Services Scope Dataset
evidence.facts: Seven vendors confirmed across clinical EHR, BI, analytics, cloud, and outsourced managed services. Confidence: 164 high, 64 medium. 89% evidence coverage.
evidence.fields: vendor, service, owning function, linked systems, contract risk, pricing basis, confidence, active/candidate status
evidence.supports: Vendor scope inventory and contract risk identification
evidence.missing: Contract values, pricing terms, and capacity utilization data absent for all seven vendors

evidence.name: Epic Managed Services Evidence (MER-V3-EVID-0070)
evidence.facts: Epic confirmed as active vendor for clinical EHR and Cogito analytics. Integration to governed lakehouse not proven. License/support terms unevidenced.
evidence.fields: vendor, service, contract risk, linked systems, evidence ID
evidence.supports: Epic scope confirmation and integration risk flagging
evidence.missing: Clarity-to-lakehouse integration design; license and support contract terms

evidence.name: Outsourced Analytics MSP Evidence (MER-V3-EVID-0074)
evidence.facts: Outsourced analytics MSP carries ~80% maintenance load across SQL marts, Tableau, Power BI, and SAS. Vendor identity and contract values not yet evidenced.
evidence.fields: vendor, service, owning function, contract risk, linked systems, evidence ID
evidence.supports: Maintenance burden quantification and capacity rebalancing decision
evidence.missing: Vendor identity, executed contract, SOW, and FTE/capacity breakdown

evidence.name: AWS and Databricks Target Platform Evidence (MER-V3-EVID-0075, MER-V3-EVID-0076)
evidence.facts: AWS confirmed as target cloud foundation; Databricks as target lakehouse. Neither has certified medallion architecture, governed semantic layer, or patient/member identity spine.
evidence.fields: vendor, service, contract risk, linked systems, evidence IDs
evidence.supports: Target platform direction confirmation and readiness gap identification
evidence.missing: Medallion architecture certification, commercial terms, and foundation readiness assessment

evidence.name: CEO/CFO/CIO Stakeholder Interview Evidence (MER-SA07-INT-EVID-0001 to -0018)
evidence.facts: CEO, CFO, and CIO all flag lakehouse, AI/LLM governance, call center optimization, cost transparency, and payment integrity as top priorities. All five are blocked by managed services and platform gaps.
evidence.fields: stakeholder, priority use case, blocking gap, decision-grade status, evidence ID
evidence.supports: Executive priority alignment and evidence-gate identification per use case
evidence.missing: Decision-grade sign-off pending evidence closure on platform, governance, and contract terms
